action: Check PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle Database and Oracle REST Data Services against the fixed versions in the vendor advisories and patch. Review which low-privilege database accounts exist.
date_note: Date the article was published; the researcher's exploits were released shortly before.
exec: Widely used databases have public proof-of-concept exploits that let low-privilege accounts run code on the server. Vendors have fixes for all five flaws, so unpatched servers are the exposure.
plain: A researcher published working code showing that a low-privilege database account can take over the server in PostgreSQL, MySQL and other databases. All five flaws have fixes.

key_findings: Researcher Zheng Yu of Depthfirst published proofs of concept for memory-corruption bugs in PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus an Oracle chain needing no login.
Four flaws have vendor CVEs and fixes; ClickHouse has no CVE and was fixed in September (26.9 and later, with backports), per The Hacker News after its 20 Nov correction.
The article says no attack in the wild has been seen and the full chains were not reproduced independently.

summary: The Hacker News reports that researcher Zheng Yu of Depthfirst published proof-of-concept exploits that let low-privilege database accounts run code on the server in PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus an Oracle chain needing no login. Four flaws have CVEs and vendor fixes; ClickHouse has no CVE but was fixed in September. No attacks in the wild are reported, and the chains were not independently reproduced.
title: Researcher publishes database RCE exploits for PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle

validation.note: Compared Depthfirst's own post (18 Nov), Brandefense (19 Nov) and The Hacker News (19 Nov): researcher chains for PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle, same CVEs, vendor fixes for the CVE-listed flaws. ClickHouse having no CVE and being fixed in September is stated only by The Hacker News (summary attributes it); neither Depthfirst nor Brandefense says exploit code is public or that no attacks were seen.

review.note: Content matches THN; ClickHouse was said to have no fix but THN (corrected 20 Nov) says fixed in September; summary, exec, plain, key findings fixed. Severity 3 stands (public PoC, widely used software).
